Which AI model is used, and how are similarity and scoring calculated?
How does this app compare photos?

• Model: Google ML Kit Face Detection — on-device, bundled in the APK, no internet needed
• First step: faces are counted in fast mode; then each face is classified with landmarks in accurate mode
• Eyes open: average of the left/right eye-open probabilities
• Facing camera: head angles (yaw/roll — headEulerAngleY/Z)
• Smile: ML Kit's smiling probability
• Natural mouth: vertical gap between upper/lower lip contours relative to mouth width — catches wide-open mouths such as mid-speech or yawning
• Runs entirely on device: no photo ever leaves your phone

1. Each photo is reduced to a small preview (for fast analysis)
2. Perceptual fingerprint (dHash): the preview is reduced to 9×8 grayscale and neighbouring pixel brightness is compared to produce a 64-bit "fingerprint"
3. Time window: only photos taken within a certain time of each other are compared — 3 minutes (180 seconds) by default, adjustable from 10 to 600 seconds in Settings
4. Hash distance: the number of differing bits (Hamming distance) between two fingerprints is checked; below the threshold counts as "visually similar" — default threshold is 10 out of 64 bits, adjustable from 4 to 16 with the "sensitivity" slider in Settings
5. Face count check: even if visually similar, two shots with a different number of people are NEVER put in the same group
6. Grouping: all photos linked by the criteria above end up in one group (transitive: if A~B and B~C, then A, B and C are in the same group)

Default relative weights: face quality 40 (within it: eyes open 45 · natural mouth 25 · smile 15 · facing camera 15) · sharpness 35 · exposure 15 · resolution 10 · people standing together 20 · clean composition 25. Criteria that don't apply to a group (e.g. face quality and togetherness in a landscape without faces) are dropped and the rest are re-normalised.

People standing together: in shots with more than one person, the distance between neighbouring faces is measured in face widths. People standing shoulder to shoulder score full marks; if one or more people stand apart from the group the score drops (the weakest link decides).

Clean composition: objects in the shot are recognised with on-device image labeling. A foreign element that appears in this shot but not in the group's other shots (a ship passing through, a car, a bird, etc.) lowers the score. Because the comparison is done at object level, a shifted framing doesn't affect the result.

If no face is detected in this shot but other shots in the group have faces, a fixed low base score is used instead of face quality.
⚙️ All ratios above can be changed under Settings > \"Best Selection Weights\".
• All analysis (hashing, sharpness/exposure measurement, face analysis) runs on your device\n• No photo or analysis result is ever sent to the internet or a server
%2$d photos in %1$d groups are ready to delete (%3$s). Tap to confirm.
📱 These are near-identical screenshots: the newest is kept, the others are marked for deletion.

• Detected automatically from the folder name/path (Screenshots…) or file name (Screenshot_…)
• Never grouped with regular photos
• Because different screens of the same app can look alike to the coarse fingerprint, strict rules apply: first at most 4 of 64 bits may differ, then a 48×96 grayscale pixel comparison excluding the status and navigation bars (at most 0.3 percent of pixels may differ noticeably)
• No face/sharpness scoring; the newest copy in each group is kept
%1$d photos in this group will be deleted (%2$s freed). Then you\'ll move on to the next group.

Android normally asks for confirmation on every delete. Grant \"Media management\" once and Best Photo Select won\'t ask again (with trash mode on, deleted photos can still be restored for 30 days).\n\nTurn the permission on for Best Photo Select on the next screen and come back. This question won\'t be shown again; you can also grant it later in Settings.
Off: WhatsApp folders are hidden, can\'t be selected and aren\'t scanned
Nothing is deleted; you\'re told how many similar groups and photos were found. Tap the notification to review them.
In each group everything except the best shot is deleted without confirmation; you\'re told how many photos were deleted and how much space was freed.
%1$d similar groups found · %2$d photos can be deleted (%3$s). Tap to review.
Pick the albums to scan and tap \"Start scan\". Similar shots are grouped and the AI picks the best one in each group.
In a group, the starred shot is kept and the ones with a red frame will be deleted. Tap a photo to inspect it full screen and change the choice.
With trash mode on, deleted photos can be restored from the phone\'s trash for 30 days. You can turn it on or off in Settings.
On the group screen, delete the marked photos and continue with \"Next group\"; \"Previous group\" takes you back.
Stop the confirmation on every delete
Grant \"Media management\" once in Settings and Android will no longer ask for a separate confirmation on every delete.
In Settings, choose \"Scan and notify\" or \"Scan and delete automatically\" to have your albums scanned daily, every 3 days or weekly.
With high sensitivity in Settings only nearly identical shots are grouped; lower it to get broader groups.
Only shots taken close together are compared (3 minutes by default). You can change it in Settings from 10 seconds to 10 minutes.
Use the weights in Settings to set how much open eyes, smiles, sharpness or people standing together matter to you.
If a shot contains a foreign element the others don\'t have, like a passing ship, a car or a bird, it gets a lower score.
Mark a group you want to keep with \"Never show again\" and it won\'t be suggested in later scans. You can reset this in Settings.
Use the theme button in the top bar of the Albums screen to choose light, dark or your phone\'s theme.
Tap the flag in the top bar to change the app\'s language; by default it uses your phone\'s language.
Use the view button in the top bar to see albums as a grid with large covers or as a compact list.
Don\'t want to scan photos received on WhatsApp? Turn off \"Show WhatsApp folders\" and they\'ll be hidden from the list.
Screenshots are never mixed with regular photos; only exact copies are grouped and the newest one is kept.
Tap the clock icon in the top bar to see the photos deleted so far.
The \"How does it work?\" page in Settings explains step by step how similarity and the best shot are calculated.

Similarity, time window, trash mode, automatic scan (turned off), \"best\" weights, theme, grid/list view and WhatsApp folders go back to their defaults. Your selected albums, ignored groups, language and history are kept.
✅ All settings are back to their defaults.
